title: Hom commutes with a telescope under two sequence-specific coproduct comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], with morphism groups small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $K\in\mathcal T$. Let $(X_n,u_n:X_n\to X_{n+1})_{n\geq0}$ be a sequence. Suppose its coproduct $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}X_n$ exists [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with coprojections $\iota_n$, and choose a distinguished triangle $B\xrightarrow{1-s}B\xrightarrow{p}H\xrightarrow{q}B[1]$, where $s\iota_n=\iota_{n+1}u_n$. Assume that both canonical maps
$$\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,X_n)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,B),\qquad
\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,X_n[1])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,B[1])$$
are bijective, where the second map uses the shifted coprojections $\iota_n[1]$. Then the canonical map of abelian groups
$$\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,X_n)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,H),\qquad [f:K\to X_n]\longmapsto p\iota_n f$$
is bijective. The colimit transitions are postcomposition with $u_n$. No compactness hypothesis for families other than these two specified families is imposed.

proof.text:
Put $A_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,X_n)$, $A_n^+=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,X_n[1])$, $D=\bigoplus_n A_n$ and $D^+=\bigoplus_n A_n^+$. Write $e_n,e_n^+$ for the direct-sum injections, and $\beta,\beta^+$ for the two assumed comparison maps. These are additive, hence are group isomorphisms by the assumed bijectivity. Define $t_n(f)=u_n\circ f$, $t_n^+(g)=u_n[1]\circ g$, and $\sigma(e_nf)=e_{n+1}t_n(f)$, $\sigma^+(e_n^+g)=e_{n+1}^+t_n^+(g)$. For $a=1-s$, the defining equation for $s$ and additivity give
$$a_*\beta(e_nf)=\iota_nf-\iota_{n+1}u_nf=\beta(1-\sigma)(e_nf).$$
The shift is additive [def-weil-triangulated-category], so $a[1]=1-s[1]$ and $s[1]\iota_n[1]=\iota_{n+1}[1]u_n[1]$. Thus also $a[1]_*\beta^+=\beta^+(1-\sigma^+)$. The displayed identities on summands imply the identities on every finite sum.

source.place: Tags 0CRK (lemma-cohomology-of-hocolim), displayed five-term sequence, and 094A (lemma-commutes-with-countable-sums): identify its first and last arrows

proof.text: The map $1-\sigma^+$ is injective by its coordinates. If $(1-\sigma^+)g=0$ for $g=(g_n)\in D^+$, its coordinate $0$ says $g_0=0$, and its coordinate $n+1$ says $g_{n+1}=t_n^+(g_n)$. Induction gives $g_n=0$ for all $n$, hence $g=0$. Conjugating by $\beta^+$ in Step 1 shows that postcomposition by $a[1]$ on $\operatorname{Hom}(K,B[1])$ is injective. This uses neither injectivity nor surjectivity of any transition $u_n$.

source.place: Tag 093W (lemma-compute-colimit), injectivity of identity minus forward shift; coordinate proof for abelian groups

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to the supplied distinguished triangle $B\xrightarrow{a}B\xrightarrow{p}H\xrightarrow{q}B[1]$. Clause (i) gives $pa=0$. Rotate twice by TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]; the first two maps are $q$ and $-a[1]$, so clause (i) also gives $a[1]q=0$. For any $h:K\to H$, Step 2 now implies $qh=0$. The once-rotated distinguished triangle has first two maps $p,q$; clause (ii) applied to it gives $h=pb$ for some $b:K\to B$. Hence $p_*$ is surjective. Clause (ii) applied to the original triangle says that $pb=0$ implies $b=ac$ for some $c:K\to B$, while $pa=0$ gives the converse. Therefore $\ker p_*=\operatorname{im}a_*$. With $\gamma=p_*\beta:D\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,H)$, Step 1 yields
$$\gamma\text{ is surjective},\qquad \ker\gamma=\operatorname{im}(1-\sigma).$$
Indeed a kernel element $d$ satisfies $\beta d=ac$; write $c=\beta c'$ to get $d=(1-\sigma)c'$ by injectivity of $\beta$.

source.place: Tags 0146 (lemma-composition-zero) and 0149 (lemma-representable-homological), applied to the telescope triangle and its rotations; Tag 0CRK displayed sequence

proof.text: Write $F_n=\operatorname{Hom}(K,X_n)$ and $L=\varinjlim_n F_n$. The equation $p(1-s)=0$ gives $p\iota_{n+1}u_n=p\iota_n$. Induction on $n\leq m$ extends this successor compatibility to every arrow of the indexing category. Thus $f\mapsto p\iota_n f$ is a cocone and induces $\phi:L\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,H)$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $\ell:D\to L$ be the sum of the canonical colimit maps and put $g=\ell\beta^{-1}:\operatorname{Hom}(K,B)\to L$. Then $g(\iota_n f)=[f]$. On a summand, $g((1-s)\iota_n f)=[f]-[u_nf]=0$ by colimit compatibility. Direct-sum induction and surjectivity of $\beta$ give $g\circ(1-s)_*=0$. By exactness from Step 3, $\ker p_*\subseteq\ker g$. Therefore the surjective homomorphism $p_*$ admits a unique descended homomorphism $\psi:\operatorname{Hom}(K,H)\to L$ with $\psi(p b)=g(b)$. Mathlib's AddMonoidHom.liftOfSurjective implements this factorization; its uniqueness determines the map independently of the chosen preimage.

source.place: Tag 093W (lemma-compute-colimit), cokernel identification; direct verification of the colimit universal property for abelian groups

proof.text: For each stage element, $\psi\phi([f])=\psi(p\iota_nf)=g(\iota_nf)=[f]$. The colimit hom-extensionality principle of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $\psi\phi=1_L$, so $\phi$ is injective. Conversely $\phi g\beta(e_nf)=p\iota_nf=p_*\beta(e_nf)$ on every summand; direct-sum induction and surjectivity of $\beta$ give $\phi g=p_*$. Since $p_*$ is surjective, every $h=pb$ equals $\phi(gb)$, so $\phi$ is surjective. Its stage formula is the defining formula for the colimit descendant. This is the quotient argument of the source expressed through the universal factorization of a surjective group homomorphism, without introducing an explicit quotient object. No additional comparison or compactness assumption is used.
